lines.text: Thirty seconds is a short video, but a great one takes planning. Today you plan, script and storyboard your own explainer.
A thirty second explainer has a hook, one main message and a clear ending.
Spoken at a normal pace, that is only about seventy to eighty words.
Every word has to earn its place.
AI can suggest a hook or a first draft of a script.
You cut it to length, put it in your own words and check every fact.
If a number has no trusted source, take it out.
A storyboard is a row of boxes, one for each shot.
Each box shows the picture, the words spoken and how many seconds it lasts.
Planning on paper saves hours of editing.
Only film or record people who have said yes, and never post a classmate without permission.
Never make a fake video or voice of a real person, like a cricket star or a teacher.
Use your own voice, or a voice tool only with an adult’s help.
Songs from films and streaming apps belong to their owners, so you cannot just add them.
Use music from Canva’s audio library or tracks that are free to use, and follow their licence.
Credit the music at the end.
We asked for a short script with no numbers we cannot check.
The hook and ending are good, but look at the middle: a big number with no source.
We cannot verify it, so it comes out of the script.
An explainer that teaches a wrong fact does more harm than good.
Each shot has a picture, the words, and its time, and the times add up to thirty seconds.
The last shot includes the credits for the music and a label for any AI help.
In Canva, each storyboard shot becomes one page of your video.
Under thirteen, your teacher builds it on the shared screen while you direct.
Your own voice, and people who said yes, are always fine.
Copying a real person’s voice, or using music you have no right to, is not.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
